skill.name: context7-efficient
skill.description: Fetches Context7 library documentation through helper scripts, then filters results into concise code examples, API signatures, and notes.
skill.summary: Fetch concise Context7 documentation with shell-based filtering for examples, signatures, and key notes.
skill.author: 92Bilal26

security_audit.summary: The main risk is local code execution: the skill launches Context7 through npx and includes a generic MCP client that can execute stdio commands with shell=True. Most markdown backtick, library-ID, and local text-filtering detections are false positives, but the package execution, arbitrary stdio command surface, JSON parameter construction, and PID-file process control require remediation.

remediation.suggestion: Pin @upstash/context7-mcp to a reviewed version, document the expected package source, and avoid auto-running remote package code during skill execution.
Replace shell=True with an argument-vector subprocess call, or restrict --stdio to a small allowlist of trusted MCP server commands.

remediation.issue: JSON parameters are assembled with string interpolation
remediation.suggestion: Build MCP parameter JSON with a JSON encoder such as Python json.dumps or jq instead of embedding raw shell variables.

remediation.issue: Predictable PID files in /tmp control process termination
remediation.suggestion: Validate the port as numeric, store PID files in a private runtime directory, verify the process command before killing it, and remove broad pkill fallback behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill runs @upstash/context7-mcp through npx -y without a pinned version or integrity control. This can execute newly published package code during documentation lookup or server startup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The npx command is hardcoded in multiple execution paths and no version pin is present. That creates a clear supply-chain execution risk.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped JSON Parameter Construction
semantic_findings.description: Shell scripts interpolate library, topic, mode, and page values directly into JSON passed to the MCP tool. Crafted quotes can corrupt JSON or change tool parameters, even though quoting reduces shell injection risk.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The values are inserted into JSON strings without a JSON encoder. Impact appears limited to tool-argument manipulation or denial of lookup, so confidence is high on the flaw but moderate on severity.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable PID File Controls Process Termination
semantic_findings.description: The start and stop scripts use a predictable PID file under /tmp and the stop script can kill that PID or use a broad pkill fallback. A stale or tampered PID file can affect unrelated user processes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file path is predictable and shared, and the stop script sends signals based on its contents. The impact is bounded by local user permissions.

content.value_statement: Library documentation can add too much context when users only need examples or signatures. This skill fetches Context7 docs and filters them into focused, lower-token summaries.
actual_capabilities: Resolves common library names to Context7-compatible library IDs.
Fetches Context7 documentation for a selected library, topic, mode, and page.
Filters raw documentation into code examples, API signatures, and important notes.
Supports direct library IDs for faster lookups when the user already knows the ID.
Provides separate code and information modes for examples or conceptual summaries.
limitations: Requires shell access, Python, Node.js, npx, and the Context7 MCP package.
Documentation quality depends on the library coverage available in Context7.
The filtering scripts can omit details that are present in the full documentation.
The included MCP client can execute stdio commands and needs careful review before use.

use_cases.title: Look Up Framework Examples
use_cases.description: Fetch focused examples for a specific framework feature without loading full documentation into the chat.

use_cases.title: Check API Signatures During Reviews
use_cases.description: Retrieve concise signatures and notes while reviewing code that depends on unfamiliar libraries.

use_cases.title: Compare Documentation Topics
use_cases.description: Query multiple topics or pages from Context7 to build a compact reference for implementation work.

prompt_templates.title: Find Basic Examples
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for a common feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use context7-efficient to fetch concise code examples for React useState.

prompt_templates.title: Get Conceptual Guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn how a framework feature works before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use context7-efficient in info mode to explain Next.js routing with the most important notes.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Known Library ID
prompt_templates.scenario: Skip library resolution when the exact Context7 ID is known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use context7-efficient with library ID /prisma/docs and topic queries. Return examples and API signatures.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Multiple Pages
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced lookup when the first page is not enough.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use context7-efficient to fetch pages 1 and 2 for React hooks, then summarize differences in the returned guidance.

output_examples.output: A compact result with several useState examples, related signatures, and a short notes section.

output_examples.input: Explain Prisma getting started in info mode.
output_examples.output: A concise overview with important setup guidance and a small number of relevant examples.

output_examples.input: Get Next.js routing docs from a known Context7 ID.
output_examples.output: A filtered reference focused on routing patterns, important notes, and API usage details.

best_practices: Use direct library IDs when they are known to reduce lookup time.
Choose code mode for implementation examples and info mode for conceptual guidance.
Review filtered output against full documentation when making high-impact changes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat filtered snippets as a complete substitute for official documentation.
Do not pass untrusted stdio commands to the bundled MCP client.
Do not rely on unpinned npx execution in locked-down or production environments.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It fetches Context7 library documentation and filters it into concise examples, signatures, and notes.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Context7 MCP tooling through npx and can also use HTTP MCP endpoints.

faq.question: Can it fetch full documentation?
faq.answer: The scripts fetch raw documentation internally, then return filtered output by default.

faq.question: Is the included MCP client safe for arbitrary commands?
faq.answer: No. The stdio mode executes a provided command and should only receive trusted commands.

faq.question: What should users verify before installing?
faq.answer: Users should review the scripts, the npx dependency, and any local execution policy requirements.
